rules.statement: Define each variant's capabilities (validation rules, generation, export support, asymmetric/public-key flags) once, in a registered descriptor looked up from a catalog, instead of repeating `switch` statements or CLR type checks on the type discriminator across several services.
rules.why: Copies of per-type knowledge kept in step by hand had already drifted; one source of truth makes it structurally impossible for generator, validator, converter and UI to disagree.
rules.check: Look for new or extended `switch`/`if` chains on a type discriminator (or `is` checks on concrete types) that decide capabilities in more than one service, or a parallel dictionary/set of valid types, where a descriptor/catalog lookup should be used.

rules.statement: Register built-in strategy/descriptor implementations with `TryAddEnumerable` so that new variants can be added by registering another implementation, without editing existing code.
rules.why: Adding a type should only mean registering a descriptor, which keeps the catalog open for extension.
rules.check: Strategy-collection registrations that use `AddSingleton`/`TryAddSingleton` for a single implementation, or hard-code the variant list inside the aggregating service, instead of `TryAddEnumerable` for each descriptor.

rules.statement: Clients and frontends must not hard-code lists of server-supported types or capabilities; get them from a server discovery/capabilities endpoint.
rules.why: A hard-coded client-side copy had already drifted from the server (it used the wrong discriminator value), and clients should learn server behavior instead of guessing it.
rules.check: Frontend or client code that adds literal sets/arrays of type names or capability flags to gate UI actions or form options, where the server publishes a capabilities document.

rules.statement: Build discovery/capabilities documents from registered contributor providers into an extension-data (`[JsonExtensionData]`) document, so a new section is published by registering a provider and not by editing the endpoint or the resource type.
rules.why: Following the OpenID discovery pattern keeps the document open for extension (algorithms, curves, future sections) without changes to the endpoint.
rules.check: Changes that add a new discovery section by adding properties to the discovery resource type or logic to the endpoint handler, instead of adding a new registered provider.

rules.statement: Put domain capability logic used by several consumers in the core abstractions layer, not in the persistence layer, and keep persisted discriminator values as a persistence concern mapped to runtime types.
rules.why: Capability logic is used by both services and management, while the persistence layer's access is restricted, and persisted discriminators (e.g. `x509`) do not have to match runtime key types.
rules.check: Domain or capability types added to a DAL/persistence project, or domain logic that branches on persisted discriminator strings instead of the deserialized runtime type.
